title: Platform systems & services playbook: runbooks, how-tos, dashboards, and roadmap
author: Maya Chen
body:
Overview

This playbook gathers the canonical platform engineering operating procedures for Redwood Inference: systems & services inventory, common how-tos, dashboards and alerts conventions, primary runbooks, recent retrospectives, and the Q1 2027 roadmap. It is intended as the team wiki entry point for oncall engineers, platform owners, and engineers building new services. Keep this page up-to-date; small changes should be made directly, larger process changes should go through PR + reviewers listed above.

1) Systems & services inventory (owner & criticality)

Summary table (service, owner, tier, SLOs, primary dashboard):
| service | owner | tier | SLO (p99 latency / availability) | dashboard |
|---|---|---:|---|---|
| routing-api | eng-serving-runtime | critical | p99 < 250ms, availability 99.95% | /dashboards/routing-api-summary |
| inference-worker | eng-serving-runtime | critical | p95 < 1200ms, availability 99.9% | /dashboards/inference-worker-ops |
| batch-ingest | eng-platform | standard | throughput 10k/min, availability 99.5% | /dashboards/batch-ingest |
| metrics-pipeline | eng-platform | critical | data-lag < 60s, availability 99.9% | /dashboards/metrics-pipeline |
| k8s-cluster-control | eng-infra | critical | control-plane availability 99.99% | /dashboards/k8s-control-plane |

Action: owners must confirm this table at the start of each quarter. Add new services by filing an ADR and updating this page.

2) How-tos (common tasks)

A. Add a new service to platform monitoring
- Overview: How to onboard a new service to dashboards, alerts, and runbooks.
- Steps:
  1. Create a metrics contract: list of metrics, labels, cardinality expectations (file: /metrics/contracts/<service>-contract.yaml).
  2. Add Prometheus exporters and register target in prometheus-static-config.
  3. Create a dashboard JSON in Grafana: follow template /grafana/templates/service-summary.json.
  4. Define alert rules (see Alerts section) and submit PR to terraform-monitoring.
  5. Add a short runbook stub under /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/<service>-oncall.
- Verification: runbook reviewer verifies dashboard links and alert ping test.

B. Deploy a constrained-sized canary for a runtime change
- Use the canary pipeline (CI job: pipeline/canary-deploy) with traffic shaping using Istio percentage rollout.
- Commands (kubectl / cicd):
  - Trigger: ./scripts/ci-trigger.sh --pipeline canary-deploy --service inference-worker --image my-image:canary
  - Route 5% traffic: kubectl apply -f k8s/canary/5pct-routing.yaml
  - Monitor: curl -sS https://grafana.redwood/example-dashboard | jq '.panels[] | select(.title=="errors")'
- Rollback: kubectl apply -f k8s/canary/rollback.yaml or trigger pipeline/rollback in CI.

3) Dashboards and alerts (standards and examples)

Dashboard standards
- Every critical service must have: Overview panel (latency, errors, throughput), Capacity panel (CPU/GPU utilization, queue depth), Dependents panel (upstream/downstream dependency errors).
- Panel refresh: 1m for critical metrics, 5m for lower-priority.

SLOs & Alerting thresholds (examples)
- Availability SLO: 99.95% monthly for critical services. Alert when 1h error budget burn > 25% or 24h burn > 50%.
- Latency alerts: p95 > target for 5m OR sustained p99 > target for 1m
- Infra alerts: node GPU memory > 85% for 10m, node disk > 80% for 5m

Example alert rule (Prometheus-style, expressed here as a snippet):
```
# Alert: InferenceWorkerHighP99Latency
expr: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(inference_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, instance)) > 1.2
for: 5m
labels:
  severity: page
annotations:
  summary: "Inference worker p99 latency high ({{ $labels.instance }})"
  runbook: "/confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/inference-worker-oncall"
```

Alerting policy & paging
- severity=page -> PagerDuty escalation (primary oncall -> secondary -> eng-sre).
- severity=ticket -> create Jira ticket in PLAT board, assign to service owner.
- All page alerts must include a runbook link label and remediation steps.

4) Platform runbooks (short actionable runbooks)

A. Inference worker OOM / GPU OOM
- Symptom: sudden spike in OOMKilled pods or container OOMs on GPU nodes.
- Immediate actions:
  1. PagerDuty -> acknowledge incident.
  2. Check pod logs: kubectl -n inference logs <pod> --previous.
  3. Inspect node OOM events: kubectl describe node <node> and dmesg on host via bastion.
  4. Scale down batch tasks: kubectl scale deployment batch-ingest --replicas=0 (if applicable).
  5. If kernel OOM across nodes, cordon & migrate pods off node: kubectl cordon <node>; kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data.
- Post-incident: complete the incident checklist, attach GPU metrics (nvidia-smi snapshots) and open a PR for any required resource limit fixes.

B. Metrics pipeline lag
- Symptom: dashboard data lag > 60s or missing panels.
- Actions:
  1. Check kafka topic lag: ./tools/kafka-monitor --topic metrics-raw --lag
  2. Restart metrics-consumer deployment: kubectl rollout restart deployment/metrics-consumer
  3. Validate Prometheus remote_write connectivity and S3 short-term bucket health.

5) Retrospectives (recent items & follow-ups)

Quarterly retrospective summary (Q4 2026)
- Issue: Increased p99 tails on routing-api after model-routing change.
- What happened: new dynamic routing rule resulted in cache miss spikes and unoptimized kernel selection for long contexts.
- Actions taken: rolled back routing rule, added cache warmup in runtime, improved kernel selection logging.
- Follow-ups (owner / ETA): eng-serving-runtime to ship cache warmup by 2027-01-15 (owner: Diego Ramos), create perf benchmark for long-context (owner: Maya Chen, ETA 2027-02-01).

Postmortem links: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/postmortem-routing-api-cache-miss-2026-11

6) Roadmap (Q1 2027 highlights)

- Q1 2027: Metrics pipeline hardening (reduce data-lag to < 30s), rollout dynamic batching autoscaler to dedicated pools, unified alerting policy migration.
- Q2 2027: Private deployment observability bundle (lightweight Grafana + aggregated logs), standardized canary tooling for model rollouts.
- Q3 2027: Autoscaling for GPU pools with proactive replenishment, SLO-based autoscaler integration.

Milestones and owners:
- Metrics pipeline hardening — owner: eng-platform (Priya Kapoor) — M1: add end-to-end integration tests (Feb), M2: backfill missing metrics (Mar), M3: cutover (Apr).
- Canary tooling polish — owner: eng-platform (Maya Chen) — remove manual steps in pipeline by Mar.

7) Team wiki & ownership

Where to find related docs:
- Runbooks: /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks
- Dashboards: Grafana (bookmark /dashboards/platform-summary)
- Oncall rota: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/rota
- ADRs and design docs: /confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records

Ownership rules
- Each service must have a named owner in the inventory above. Owners are responsible for SLO definition, runbook accuracy, and responding to review requests.
- Platform oncall is rotated weekly; platform incidents should be classified and handed off to service owner for follow-up.

8) Maintenance & housekeeping checklist (quarterly)
- Verify dashboard links and alert runbook references (owners).
- Audit metrics cardinality (owners & eng-platform).
- Run load-test smoke (dev & staging) against canary pipelines.
- Archive stale runbooks and decommissioned dashboards (eng-platform).

Appendix: useful commands and snippets
- Prometheus query to surface top services by p99 latency:
  sort_desc(histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, service)))
- Grafana export/import:
  grafana-cli dashboards export --id=<id> --output=./dash.json
- CI Canary trigger (example):
  ./scripts/ci-trigger.sh --pipeline canary-deploy --service inference-worker --image registry.redwood/release:canary-202702

If anything on this page is out-of-date, please file a PR or ping the reviewers listed at the top.
